analysis.investment_thesis: City Union Bank, founded in 1904 and operating for over 120 years, exhibits the consistency of earnings I respect: net profit has grown from INR 760 Cr to INR 1,124 Cr over four years at a 13.9% CAGR with OCF positive all four years. However, at P/E 15.3 (barely above my 15× ceiling) and P/B 1.92 (above my 1.5× ceiling), the price exceeds my required margin of safety — I would need a more attractive entry point.
key_strengths: 120-year operating history with unbroken profitability: net profit grew every single year in the four-year data series — INR 760, 937, 1,016, 1,124 Cr — the kind of steady, boring consistency I admire
Improving book value: total equity compounded from INR 6,586 Cr (2022) to INR 9,467 Cr (2025) while borrowings (non-deposit debt) fell sharply from INR 5,312 Cr to INR 1,790 Cr
Forward P/E of 12.5× suggests the market expects continued earnings growth, which if realised would bring valuation into a more acceptable range
key_risks: P/B of 1.92 exceeds my maximum of 1.5 — for a regional bank with limited pricing power and geographic concentration in South India, this premium is hard to justify
Finance costs rising at 17.2% CAGR (INR 2,188 Cr to INR 3,518 Cr) reflect rising deposit costs that could squeeze net interest margins in a sustained high-rate environment
OCF was weak in FY24 (INR 436 Cr) versus INR 1,166 Cr in FY22 — banking OCF is volatile and the recent INR 1,128 Cr recovery in FY25 may not be sustained
red_flags: P/B of 1.92 breaches my 1.5× ceiling — I am reluctant to pay nearly twice book for any bank, however well-managed
Revenue growth of only 6.3% CAGR over three years is tepid for a bank that needs to grow its loan book to justify the current valuation
analysis.detailed_analysis:
City Union Bank is precisely the type of institution I appreciate: old, conservative, and consistently profitable. A 120-year track record eliminates the single greatest concern I have with most modern businesses — that management has not been tested by adversity. Net profits have grown every year in the available data, equity has compounded solidly, and non-deposit borrowings have been cut by two-thirds. These are marks of prudent stewardship.

Nevertheless, at INR 257.8, the stock does not offer the margin of safety I demand. P/E of 15.3 sits exactly at my ceiling; P/B of 1.92 exceeds it by nearly 30%. For a bank with a geographically concentrated franchise and modest loan growth, I require a discount to book — not a premium. I would study this bank closely for an entry nearer 1.2–1.3× book, which would represent the kind of bargain Mr. Market occasionally offers to the patient investor.
